video.description:
Learn to explain how to add symbol animations, haptic feedback and gradients in SwiftUI: symbolEffect, sensoryFeedback & MeshGradient, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
symbolEffect - A modifier that animates an SF Symbol, for example with a bounce or a pulse.
sensoryFeedback - A modifier that plays a haptic or a sound when a value changes.
MeshGradient - A view that blends colors smoothly across a grid of points.

landscape.hook: Can you explain symbolEffect, sensoryFeedback and MeshGradient in English?

dialogue.title: A bell that pulses

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the notification bell on my screen looks flat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add symbolEffect. It animates an SF Symbol, for example with a pulse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can it react when something happens?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, give symbolEffect a value, and it runs when the value changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. When the user taps save, I want a small vibration.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use sensoryFeedback with the `saved` value. When `saved` changes, the phone plays a haptic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used an old feedback generator before. It needed more code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, sensoryFeedback is shorter, and it stays in SwiftUI.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One more thing. The login screen needs a soft color background.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Try a MeshGradient. It blends colors across a grid of points.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is a MeshGradient slower than a normal gradient?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A bit, so keep the grid small, like two by two.

dialogue.code:
let saved = false
Image(systemName: "bell")
    .symbolEffect(.pulse)
    .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: saved)
